short: The most inventive and commercially advanced state in the medieval world, and the least secure.
full:
Zhao Kuangyin, having taken power in 960 in a military coup, spent his reign making another one impossible: generals were pensioned off, armies rotated away from their commanders, and civil officials recruited by competitive examination placed permanently above them. What followed was an economic transformation. Early-ripening Champa rice allowed double cropping, the iron industry reached outputs Europe would not match for six centuries, and merchants used printed paper money, letters of credit, the magnetic compass at sea and gunpowder weapons on land. Kaifeng became a city of a million people supplied entirely by trade.

Military weakness shadowed all of it. The Song paid annual tribute in silver and silk to the Khitan Liao and the Tangut Xi Xia, and in 1127 the Jurchen Jin took Kaifeng and carried off two emperors. The court re-established itself at Lin'an, modern Hangzhou, and the Southern Song held the Yangtze line for another century and a half. Mongol armies broke through in the 1270s, and the last Song resistance ended at sea in 1279.
